answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to complete a randomly assigned, time-bounded task using a scarce resource, such as a small stake locked until its answer is checked against a hidden test. Tasks can vary from a sonnet to a zephyr forecast, while a pulse of unpredictable challenges prevents replaying one solution. This does not make sybils impossible, but each identity now costs real capital and computation, and failed or duplicated work risks forfeiting the stake, making mass identities expensive to sustain.
